name: Persistent Eustachian Valve

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Persistent Eustachian Valve

criteria.description: Visualization of a prominent membranous structure at the junction of the inferior vena cava and right atrium on echocardiography
Demonstration of failure of regression of the fetal eustachian valve remnant
Exclusion of other right atrial masses such as thrombus, tumor, or Chiari network
Presence of associated clinical features such as right atrial flow disturbance or paradoxical embolism

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Visualization of the persistent eustachian valve on echocardiography with exclusion of other right atrial masses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily imaging-based; clinical symptoms are often absent or nonspecific.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Right atrial membranous structure visualized on echocardiography
searchTerms: membrane seen in right atrium on echo

pathognomonic.symptomName: Paradoxical embolism due to right-to-left shunting
pathognomonic.notes: Occurs in cases with associated atrial septal defect or patent foramen ovale
searchTerms: blood clots passing from right to left heart
embolism caused by abnormal heart blood flow

common.notes: May cause turbulent flow detectable on Doppler imaging
searchTerms: abnormal blood flow in right atrium
turbulent blood movement in right heart chamber

common.notes: Stroke without identifiable cause, possibly linked to embolism
Occasional arrhythmias related to atrial irritation

occasional.notes: Due to impaired right atrial filling or shunting

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac efficiency
searchTerms: fatigue due to decreased cardiac output
low energy related to heart inefficiency

occasional.notes: Atrial fibrillation or flutter may occur
searchTerms: abnormal heart rhythm from right atrium
heart murmur from turbulent blood flow
abnormal heart sounds due to flow disturbance

rare.notes: In severe cases with significant flow obstruction
searchTerms: swelling and fatigue from right heart failure

rare.notes: Rare embolic events possibly linked to valve morphology
searchTerms: blood clots causing systemic embolism without heart shunt

rare.symptomName: Infective endocarditis of the eustachian valve
searchTerms: infection of eustachian valve in heart
heart valve infection in eustachian valve

imaging: Echocardiographic visualization of persistent membranous structure at inferior vena cava-right atrium junction
Doppler evidence of right atrial flow disturbance
other: Clinical history of cryptogenic stroke or paradoxical embolism
Exclusion of other right atrial masses

distinguishingFeatures: Mobile, net-like structure in right atrium
Associated with hypercoagulable states or atrial fibrillation
May coexist with persistent eustachian valve

redFlags: Sudden onset neurological deficits suggesting embolic stroke
Signs of right heart failure or severe arrhythmia
references: Katz WE, et al. Persistent Eustachian Valve: Clinical and Echocardiographic Features. J Am Soc Echocardiogr. 2018.
Mayo Clinic Proceedings: Cardiac Embolism and Eustachian Valve Abnormalities, 2020
